title: How Does ChatGPT Turn Your Question Into an Answer?

facts.label: Characters of English text in one token, roughly

beats.say: A question you type into ChatGPT on your phone sets off billions of multiplications on a chip in a data centre, far from you.

place: a phone on a desk at night, a chat app open, a question being typed
a graphics chip on its board in a dark server, lighting up

moments.what: a thumb types the question into the chat box, letters appearing
the send arrow lights and the question bubble jumps up
a pulse of light leaves the top of the phone
sparks race along the phone's edge
cut to a graphics chip on its board in the dark
its surface lights in a grid of tiny squares
server racks glow behind it
the chip pulses brighter

params.question: Why is the sky blue?

beats.say: That chip sends the answer back in small pieces, and every single piece takes the whole trip through the model.

params.place: a data-centre hall: rows of server racks, light pulses running out along a cable to the phone

moments.what: rows of racks blink in a dark hall
a pulse runs out of a rack along a glowing cable
small pulses follow one after another
one pulse loops back into the rack
a ring of light runs round the rack and out again
the racks flare together

beats.say: Here is the whole trip. Your words get cut into tokens, the tokens turn into numbers, and the numbers climb through the model's layers.

params.place: a long dark table laid out like a map: six lit stations joined by a glowing track

moments.what: a glowing track draws across the table
the phone station lights
a little blade station lights
small tiles slide out of it
a station of number bars lights
a tower of layers lights
a dot climbs the tower

beats.say: A chip does the multiplying, one next word comes out, and then the whole trip starts again for the word after it.

params.place: the same map table: the chip station, the picker, and the track looping back

moments.what: the track glows
the chip station lights
its grid twinkles
a picker station pops one tile up
the tile rides back along the track
the whole track lights as a loop
a second tile starts round

beats.say: We'll follow GPT-three, an earlier model that OpenAI described in a research paper, with {fact1} parameters. Newer chatbots are built on the same idea.

params.place: a lectern at the head of the map table with the research paper open on it

moments.what: the paper lies open under a lamp
the lamp clicks on over it
its pages turn
a plate on the cover lights
the lamp over the paper brightens
a seal lights on its cover
the parameter count glows on the page
the map table lights behind it
a pulse runs the track again

beats.say: First stop: what does the model actually read? Not letters, and not quite words either.

params.place: a cutting bench: your question laid out as a glowing strip of letters under a hanging blade

moments.what: the question lies on the bench as a glowing strip
a scan line runs along it
the letters lift apart one by one
they fall back into place
the words light in turn

beats.say: Your question is cut into tokens: common chunks of text, like a whole short word, or a piece of a longer one.

params.place: the cutting bench, the blade coming down between the chunks

moments.what: the strip slides under the blade
the blade drops and slices the strip
the pieces separate into tiles
each tile lights a new colour
a short word sits on one tile
a long word splits across two tiles

beats.say: In English, a token is about {fact2} characters long on average, according to OpenAI.

params.place: the bench, one tile under a ruler marked in characters

moments.what: a ruler slides in beside one tile
its marks light one by one
the figure lands on the ruler
the other tiles line up under the ruler
the source line appears

beats.say: OpenAI also puts one token at roughly {tok_pct} of an English word, so a long answer can run to hundreds of tokens.

params.place: the bench, a word tile and a token tile side by side, then a long row of tiles

moments.what: a word tile and a smaller token tile side by side
the token tile fills part of the word tile
the share lands on the word tile
the word tile glows
tiles pour out along the bench
the row runs off the end of the bench
the whole row lights

beats.say: Why chunks, and not whole words? A common word is often a single token, while a rare word or a name gets cut into several pieces, so any word can still be built from pieces on the list.

params.place: the bench: one common word on one tile, a rare word chopped into three

moments.what: a common word slides in on one tile
it stays whole
a long rare word slides under the blade
a name follows it
the blade chops them into small pieces

beats.say: The cutting follows a fixed list of chunks that was settled before the model was trained, so the same text is always cut the same way.

params.place: a wall of drawers behind the bench, each drawer holding one chunk

moments.what: a wall of drawers lights behind the bench
a lock clicks across the wall
drawers slide open one after another
the wall glows steady
the same strip slides in again
it is cut at exactly the same places
each cut lights green

beats.say: Every chunk on that list has its own ID number, and that number is all the model is handed for each token.

params.place: the tiles on the bench, a tag clipping onto each one, a chute carrying the tags away

moments.what: the tiles sit in a row
a tag clips onto each tile
a bar code lights on each tag
the words fade off the tiles, only tags left
the tags drop into a chute
they slide away down it

beats.say: But an ID is only a label. It says nothing about what the word means. So how does a label become meaning?

params.place: a single tag in close-up on the empty bench

moments.what: one tag hangs alone over the bench
its bar code dims
the bench around it empties
a question mark rises beside it
a soft glow waits at the end of the chute

beats.say: Next stop: the model looks each ID up in a giant table and pulls out a long list of numbers for that token.

params.place: a vast lit table of glowing bars, like an archive, a tag arriving at one row

moments.what: a huge table of glowing rows stretches into the dark
a tag slides up to the table
the rows light from near to far
one row slides out
it stands up as a column of bars
the column settles above its tag

beats.say: So who chose those numbers? Nobody, by hand. Training set them, nudging each one a tiny bit at a time across enormous amounts of text.

params.place: the column of bars, pages of text streaming past it

moments.what: the column of bars stands lit
a hand outline fades away
pages of text stream past
the bars twitch up and down
a single bar shifts a hair
pages pour by in a blur

beats.say: Each list works like a point in a space with thousands of directions, and tokens used in similar ways end up close together.

params.place: a dark space full of glowing points, the column shrinking into one of them

moments.what: the column shrinks into a single point
it glows as a dot
thousands of dots fill the dark around it
faint axes run off in many directions
dots drift toward each other in clumps
the clumps tighten

beats.say: Cat lands near dog. Paris lands near London. Nobody placed them there; training did.

params.place: inside the point cloud: two pairs of labelled points side by side

moments.what: dots drift in the dark
a dot lights as cat
a dot beside it lights as dog
another dot lights as Paris
London lights beside it
a pulse joins each pair

beats.say: And how does it know which word came first? Each token also gets a second list added, marking its place in the sentence, because the order of words changes what they mean.

params.place: the row of columns back on the table, a numbered strip sliding under them

moments.what: the token columns stand in a row
a second strip of bars slides under each
the two merge and the bars change height
slot marks light under the row
two columns swap places
their bars shift as they move

beats.say: Now your question is a row of number lists. What happens to them next is where almost all the work is done.

params.place: the row of columns lifting off the table toward a tall dark shape

moments.what: the row of columns glows
the question appears above it
the row lifts off the table
a tall dark tower looms behind
its first floor lights

beats.say: Next stop, the layers. Why does a model need so many of them?

params.place: the foot of a tall glass tower of thin floors, the row of columns at its base

moments.what: the glass tower stands dark
its floors light one after another up the tower
a question mark rises
the floors keep lighting, out of sight

beats.say: GPT-three stacks dozens of these layers, one on top of the next, and the row of number lists passes through every single one, in order.

params.place: the glass tower from the side, the row of columns rising floor by floor

moments.what: the tower stands lit
a plate at its base lights with the model's name
the floors press together
the row of columns enters the first floor
the row rises through floor after floor
a glow climbs with it

beats.say: On a single floor, what comes first? Every token looks back at the tokens before it, and takes in a little of what they carry.

params.place: one floor up close: the columns in a row, glowing threads reaching back from each to the earlier ones

moments.what: one floor, the columns in a row
the last column lights
threads reach back from it to the earlier columns
every column reaches back the same way
light flows along the threads
each column takes on a tint from the others

beats.say: That is how blue in your question can take on the meaning of a colour, not a mood, from the words around it.

params.place: the same floor: the column for blue between sky and the others, threads lighting to sky

moments.what: the column for blue lights
the question shows above the row
a thick thread lights from sky to blue
a faint thread to a mood fades out
the blue column turns sky blue

beats.say: Then each token's list goes through a block of multiplications on its own, and its numbers come out slightly changed.

params.place: the floor: each column passing through a lit block of switches

moments.what: the columns stand after the threads fade
a lit block rises in front of each column
each column passes through its block
sparks fly inside the blocks
the bars come out at new heights
they settle

beats.say: Floor after floor, the lists change a little each time. By the top, a list no longer stands for one word. It carries what the whole sentence is about.

params.place: the tower from below, the row climbing, glow brightening at the top

moments.what: the row climbs floor after floor
the bars shift a little on each floor
the row reaches the top floor
the word on the last column fades
its bars blend with the others' colours
the top of the tower glows

beats.say: The multiplying on every floor uses numbers stored inside the model, called parameters. And that is where size comes in.

params.place: the tower's walls opening to show shelves of tiny glowing beads behind every floor

moments.what: a floor with its blocks
the walls fill with tiny glowing beads
shelves of beads line every floor
the beads pulse together
the beads spread up the whole tower

beats.say: Because those parameters have to be multiplied somewhere, by something you can touch. That is where the software meets the hardware.

params.place: the tower fading to a glass outline, a real chip glowing at its foot

moments.what: the tower glows
it fades to a glass outline
a chip appears glowing at its foot
the chip lights brighter
the tower sinks into the chip

beats.say: So where does all this multiplying actually happen? In a data centre, on racks of servers packed with graphics chips.

params.place: the data-centre hall, a rack opening to show its boards of graphics chips

moments.what: rows of racks hum in the hall
a question mark floats in the aisle
aisle lights run down the hall
a rack slides open
its boards glide out
the graphics chips on them light up

beats.say: GPT-three has {fact1} parameters, and every one of them is used in a multiplication for every single token it writes.

params.place: a graphics chip on its board, close, a counter on the board edge

moments.what: the chip sits on its board, memory stacks beside it
a plate by the chip lights
the parameter count lands on a plate by the chip
a stream of beads pours into the chip
the chip's surface lights in a grid
one token tile lights at the side
the chip flashes

beats.say: Those numbers are the model. There is no list of facts inside it, only parameters, set during training.

params.place: the chip's memory stacks lit, beads streaming, an empty shelf where a book would be

moments.what: the memory stacks glow
beads swirl above them
a book outline appears
it dissolves into beads
the beads line up in a grid
they settle into the stacks

beats.say: Inside the chip, what does the work? Thousands of tiny maths units. Each one multiplies two numbers and adds the result to a running total.

params.place: inside the chip: a grid of small maths units, one in close-up taking two numbers

moments.what: the chip's surface opens into a grid of tiny units
the units light row by row
two beads fly into one unit
they meet in the unit
the unit flashes
its running total bar grows

beats.say: They all work at once, so a whole grid of numbers is multiplied in one sweep, and a chip like this does hundreds of trillions of them every second.

params.place: the grid of maths units, a wave of light sweeping across it

moments.what: the grid of units waits
every unit lights together
a wave sweeps across the grid
another wave follows
waves run so fast they blur
the chip glows white

beats.say: Where do the parameters wait? In memory stacked right beside the chip, and they stream into those maths units over and over, token after token.

params.place: the board: tall memory stacks beside the chip, streams of beads running into it

moments.what: the memory stacks stand beside the chip
their layers light
a bridge of wires lights between them and the chip
beads stream across the bridge
the stream repeats
a token tile lights each time the stream passes

beats.say: A model this big is usually split across several chips, passing numbers back and forth between them over fast links.

params.place: several chips side by side on boards, glowing links between them

moments.what: one chip with its memory
its memory overflows with beads
the beads split off to more chips sliding in
a row of chips lights
pulses run between them
the links glow

beats.say: All that switching turns into heat, which is why data centres need so much power, and so much cooling.

params.place: the hall: hot air rising off the racks, cooling pipes and fans

moments.what: the racks glow
sparks flicker inside
the racks glow orange, heat shimmering above
power lines light overhead
blue cooling pipes light and fans spin

beats.say: So far: words became tokens, tokens became numbers, the numbers climbed the layers, and a chip did the maths. And all of that makes just one token.

params.place: the map table again, the stations lighting in turn, then one tile at the end

moments.what: the track glows
the phone station lights
the blade station lights
the number station lights
the tower lights
the chip station lights
one tile pops up at the end
the tile glows alone

beats.say: One token? Out of everything it could say, how does it choose?

params.place: a dark stage full of token tiles on stalks, like a field of signs

moments.what: a field of token tiles on stalks lies dark
the tiles light up across the field
a question mark rises
the stalks start to grow

beats.say: The top layer gives a score to every token on the list, tens of thousands of them, for how well each would fit next.

params.place: the field of tile stalks, each stalk rising to its score

moments.what: the tiles sit low
every stalk rises to its own height
the field stretches far into the dark
a few stalks rise far above the rest
the tallest glow

beats.say: For the first word of an answer about the blue sky, tokens like Sunlight or Because score high, and banana scores almost nothing.

params.place: close on the tallest stalks: The and Sunlight high, banana down in the dark

moments.what: the tall stalks stand lit
a stalk labelled Sunlight rises high
Because rises beside it
they glow
a banana tile sits low in the dark
it dims

beats.say: Then one token is picked, usually one of the likely ones, with a little randomness, which is why the same question can get a different answer.

params.place: a spinning pointer over the tall stalks, landing on one

moments.what: the tall stalks
a pointer spins over them
it slows over the tallest
it wobbles between two
it lands on one
a ghost pointer lands on the other

beats.say: That token is added to the end of the text, and the model reads your question plus the new token, and makes the whole trip again.

params.place: the picked tile flying to the end of the sentence strip, the strip sliding back toward the tower

moments.what: the picked tile glows
it flies to the end of the sentence strip
it clicks into place
the question glows on the strip
the new tile flashes
the strip slides back toward the tower

beats.say: Up through every layer, once more, just to pick the token after that. Then again. And again.

params.place: the field and the strip, tiles flying in one after another, the stalks rising each time

moments.what: the stalks rise again
a pulse runs up from the tower
the field flickers
another tile flies to the strip
another
and another, faster

beats.say: That is why you see the answer appear piece by piece. You are watching it being written, one token at a time.

params.place: the strip of answer tiles growing, a phone screen frame around it

moments.what: the answer strip glows
a phone screen frame forms around it
tiles pop on one by one
a cursor blinks at the end
another tile pops on
and another

beats.say: Doesn't that waste time? To save it, the chip keeps notes about the earlier tokens in its memory, so it doesn't redo all of their maths from the beginning.

params.place: the strip of tiles, each old tile dropping a small glowing note into a tray below

moments.what: the tiles sit in the strip
a little clock spins
each old tile drops a glowing note into a tray
the tray lights
the old tiles dim, already done
only the newest tile lights

beats.say: It ends when the token it picks is a special one that means stop.

params.place: the field, one plain dark tile rising to the top, the strip closing

moments.what: the stalks rise
a plain dark tile rises highest
the pointer lands on it
it flashes red
the strip closes with a click

beats.say: So does it look your answer up? Not on its own. Unless the app gives it a search tool, it predicts each next token from patterns it learned.

params.place: the field of stalks with an empty, unlit bookshelf at its edge

moments.what: the stalks stand
an empty bookshelf appears at the edge
it stays dark
a magnifier tool slides in and out
the stalks rise again
the whole field glows

beats.say: That is why it can sound sure and still be wrong. A likely-sounding token isn't always a true one.

params.place: close on two tall stalks: one green, one that turns red

moments.what: two tall stalks side by side
both glow bright
one turns red
they stay the same height
the other gets a green tick

beats.say: But there is a limit to how much text it can look back on while it writes. And GPT-three's limit was small.

params.place: a long conveyor of tiles running through a lit frame, the frame's edges glowing

moments.what: a long belt of tiles runs into the dark
a lit frame drops over part of it
tiles inside it light up
its edges glow
the belt moves under it
slot marks light along the frame
the frame pulls in

beats.say: GPT-three could read only a limited number of tokens at once, called its window. It held your question, everything said before it, and the answer so far.

params.place: the belt under the frame, the slot count on the frame, three coloured stretches of tiles inside it

moments.what: the frame lights over the belt
slot marks light along the frame
tiles fill the frame
the question stretch lights cyan
the earlier chat lights amber
the answer so far lights white

beats.say: At about {fact2} characters a token, that window held only a few pages of text, not a whole book.

params.place: beside the frame: a few pages, and a thick book that doesn't fit

moments.what: the frame of tiles
the characters figure lands on a tile
a few pages slide out of the frame
a thick book drops beside it
the book glows red at the frame's edge

beats.say: And what happens to anything older? It drops out of the window. The model simply can't see it any more, as if it was never said.

params.place: the belt moving, old tiles sliding out of the frame's back edge and falling into the dark

moments.what: the belt moves forward
the oldest tiles reach the frame's back edge
they drop off into the dark
they go grey
they vanish
the frame holds only the newest tiles

beats.say: It doesn't remember you between chats either, unless the app copies your earlier messages back into the window.

params.place: two chat bubbles on either side of the frame, a hand-off arrow carrying old messages back in

moments.what: the frame sits empty
an empty chat bubble fades
a second chat bubble appears
an arrow lights from the old chat
old message tiles ride back along it
they drop into the frame

beats.say: Newer models have far bigger windows, but the rule is the same: if it isn't in the window, the model doesn't see it.

params.place: the frame stretching longer along the belt, tiles outside it still dark

moments.what: the frame over the belt
the frame stretches far along the belt
its far edge glows
tiles outside it stay dark
they fade further

beats.say: Now follow it back out. The picked token leaves the chip, crosses the data centre, and travels the network to your phone.

params.place: the hall, a single light pulse leaving a rack and running down the cable out of the hall

moments.what: the racks hum
one pulse lights in a rack
it leaves the rack
it runs down the aisle
it races along the cable
it disappears into the distance

beats.say: On your screen it lands as a few letters. Then the next one arrives, and the next, faster than you can read.

params.place: the phone on the desk again, the answer filling the chat bubble

moments.what: the phone glows on the desk
a pulse arrives at the phone
a few letters appear in the bubble
more letters follow
and more
the bubble fills quickly

params.question: Why is the sky blue?
params.answer: Sunlight scatters off the air, and blue light scatters the most.

beats.say: So in GPT-three, every token of an answer is a fresh vote among tens of thousands of tokens, cast by {fact1} numbers, multiplied on a chip.

params.place: the chip again, its grid lighting, the field of stalks ghosted above it

moments.what: the chip's grid glows
a token tile appears over it
a ghost field of stalks rises above the chip
beads stream in
the parameter count lights on the board
the chip flashes
the count pulses
the grid flashes
the chip glows white

beats.say: Which step should we take apart next? Tell us. And next time you type a question, watch the first word arrive.

params.place: the phone on the desk, a new question being typed, as at the start

moments.what: the phone on the desk
the screen glows
a comment bubble pops
a thumb types a new question
the send arrow lights
a pulse leaves the phone

params.question: Why is the sky blue?
